memory.guide.label: When cleaning helps
memory.guide.title: When cleaning helps, and when it does not
memory.guide.helps.body: right after a game, an editor or an AI model that held a lot of memory has closed and something else needs a large amount at once, or when you want a clean starting point to measure from.
memory.guide.doesNot.body: just because the standby number is large. Standby memory is a cache: Windows gives it back by itself the moment a program asks for memory, so it is not wasted. Emptying it makes the next things you open load from disk, which is slower. Cleaning also does not speed up a PC that has too little memory for what it runs, and it does not fix a program that keeps growing.
